security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, local networking examples, protected secret mounts, and exclusion rules. Context review found mutable CI action references and distroless examples that may run as root. No prompt injection or credential exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: CI examples use mutable action references.
remediation.suggestion: Pin every GitHub Action to a reviewed full commit SHA and use dependency automation to propose controlled updates.

remediation.issue: Distroless examples may run application processes as root.
remediation.suggestion: Use the nonroot image variant or set a numeric USER, then verify the runtime UID in the generated container.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable CI Action References
semantic_findings.description: CI examples reference actions through mutable branch or version tags. An upstream tag change can execute altered code in privileged workflow jobs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly use @master, @v3, and @v5 instead of immutable commit SHAs. Mutable workflow references are a well-established CI supply-chain risk.

semantic_findings.title: Distroless Examples May Run as Root
semantic_findings.description: The examples claim unqualified distroless images run as non-root, but they omit USER and do not select a nonroot image variant. Generated containers may run as root.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both examples use the default distroless tag while asserting non-root behavior. Distroless publishes a separate nonroot variant, and neither example sets USER.

content.user_title: Containerize Applications for Docker and Kubernetes
content.value_statement: Container configuration is easy to misalign across local and production environments. This skill creates Dockerfiles, Compose setups, Helm structures, and security checks.
actual_capabilities: Creates multi-stage Dockerfile patterns for FastAPI and Next.js applications.
Structures Docker Compose services with networking, environment variables, dependencies, and health checks.
Outlines Helm charts with deployments, services, configuration, secrets, ingress, and resource limits.
Explains browser, server, container, CORS, startup, and health-check configuration differences.
Recommends image scanning, SBOM generation, secret mounts, and reduced container attack surfaces.
limitations: The skill provides patterns and guidance but does not deploy or operate containers automatically.
Generated configuration requires review for each application's ports, commands, dependencies, and secret sources.
The examples do not cover every language runtime, cloud provider, or Kubernetes policy.
Security claims and image defaults require verification against current upstream documentation.

use_cases.title: Package a Web Application
use_cases.description: Create coordinated Dockerfiles and Compose services for a frontend, API, database, and health checks.

use_cases.title: Prepare Kubernetes Packaging
use_cases.description: Translate container requirements into a Helm chart structure with services, configuration, ingress, and resource limits.

use_cases.title: Strengthen Container Builds
use_cases.description: Review image stages, runtime users, secret handling, vulnerability scans, and software bill of materials generation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production Dockerfile for my [runtime] application. It starts with [command], listens on [port], and installs dependencies from [file].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Compose Environment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create Docker Compose configuration for [services]. Include internal networking, environment placeholders, health checks, startup dependencies, and persistent storage where required.

prompt_templates.title: Package with Helm
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Helm chart for [application]. Include deployments, services, ingress, configuration, secret references, probes, resource limits, and environment-specific values.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Container Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my container files for image provenance, root execution, leaked secrets, unsafe networking, missing probes, mutable tags, and deployment reliability risks.

output_examples.input: Containerize a FastAPI service that uses PostgreSQL and listens on port 8000.
output: A multi-stage Python image with a non-root runtime user.
A Compose service connected to PostgreSQL through its internal service name.
A loopback health check with startup timing and database dependency guidance.

output_examples.input: Prepare a Next.js frontend and API for Kubernetes deployment.
output: Separate frontend and API image plans with build-time and runtime variables.
A Helm structure covering deployments, services, ingress, probes, and limits.
Notes for browser URLs, internal service discovery, CORS, and secret references.

output_examples.input: Review an existing container build for production security.
output: Findings for runtime users, image tags, build context, secrets, and package installation.
Recommended vulnerability scanning, signature verification, and software bill of materials checks.
Prioritized changes with deployment-specific validation steps.

best_practices: Pin base images and CI actions to reviewed immutable references.
Use multi-stage builds, non-root runtime users, minimal images, and explicit health checks.
Keep secrets outside images and pass them through dedicated secret mechanisms.
anti_patterns: Do not place credentials, environment files, or private keys in build contexts.
Do not use localhost for communication between separate containers.
Do not deploy mutable latest tags or assume an image runs as non-root.

faq.question: Which application stacks are included?
faq.answer: The examples cover FastAPI, Next.js, and general container workflows. Adapt package commands and runtime details for other stacks.

faq.question: Does the skill run Docker or Kubernetes commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides configuration patterns and command guidance. Users must review and execute commands in their own environments.

faq.question: Are generated files production ready?
faq.answer: They are starting points. Validate images, ports, users, secrets, probes, resources, network policy, and deployment requirements before release.

faq.question: How should build secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use BuildKit secret mounts or platform secret stores. Never copy secret files into image layers or commit them.

faq.question: Can it create Helm charts?
faq.answer: It outlines chart structure and common values for deployments, services, configuration, secrets, ingress, probes, and resource limits.

faq.question: Does it include security scanning guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Trivy scanning, SBOM generation, image signatures, minimal images, non-root execution, and sensitive build-context exclusions.
